decisions.text: the values are not far from zero compared with their spread
each line its own colour, handed out top to bottom by the line ends: Brackley Hill slot 1, Elstead Park slot 2, Corwen Road slot 3, Dunmore slot 4

each line labelled at its end, in the text grey, packed in order: Brackley Hill moved 0.45 line heights, Corwen Road moved 0.26 line heights, Dunmore moved 0.78 line heights, Elstead Park moved 0.59 line heights
no point markers: no value is isolated and no straight run hides one
highlighted, twice as thick, in the strong shade of its hue, its label bold: Elstead Park; the others keep their colours and widths
the unit phrase on the top label: “£500 million (monthly sales)”; the top gridline starts after it
digits hidden: millions, stated once on the top label (R2-05, D-3): “£500 million (monthly sales)”
time axis: the first and last labels kept 3 pt clear of the outer dividers, centred on their slots, which start 4.7 pt in from the left divider and end 4.4 pt before the right one
time axis: row 1 full, every third label, restarting in each group
time axis: “Jan” (Jan. 2026) closer than 3 pt to the divider between two groups: kept on its slot, with a halo in the page colour round its letters, which interrupts the divider
time axis on two levels: row 2 2025, 2026, dividers between the groups
the title wraps onto two lines
comment 1 (“New competitor garden store opened ≈ 1…”) in empty space inside the plot, 1 arrow to elstead_park at 2026-03 (G8.7)
the maker's comments in New Computer Modern italic, in the reserved blue, set apart from the labelling and outside its count of text styles (G6.3, D-19)
the four questions answered: what matters: the title; why care: comment 1 (not answered: what explains it, what to do, which need be answered only where known) (G8.3)

findings.message: the values are given in thousands (given_in thousands), yet the largest, 413,849, has 6 integer digits: it stands for £413,849,000, and the scale will read in millions. If the values are the actual amounts, leave given_in out: the generator hides digits by itself (G6.11). If they really are in thousands, say so in reasons["data.measure.unit.given_in"]
findings.title: hidden digits never mistaken: the unit the data are written in (unit.given_in) agrees with the values

source.shows: monthly sales given in pounds, as the data are: the generator hides the digits itself (“£500K”); the variant gives unit.given_in thousands as if it meant “show it in thousands”, which would read “£500 million”, and is reported (R5-11)
